posts.text: An octopus has three hearts, and the one that feeds the body stops beating whenever it swims.
comments: Which is most of why they crawl instead. Swimming is exhausting when it costs you a heartbeat.
Send it to whoever insists octopuses are just clever squid → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/three-hearts-of-love/

posts.text: Corn snakes are one of the hardier pet snakes, and nearly every health problem they develop traces back to husbandry rather than bad luck. Respiratory infection is the common one, and it is almost always secondary to an enclosure that is too cold or too damp.
comments: It needs a reptile vet and prescription antibiotics, not a wait-and-see. Full list of what to watch for → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/corn-snake-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: A sloth can hold its breath underwater for 40 minutes. A dolphin cannot.
comments: It drops its heart rate to a third of normal to stretch the oxygen. The slowness is the whole strategy.
Worth firing at the next person who calls sloths lazy → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/breath-holding-sloths/

posts.text: A narwhal's tusk is not a horn. It is a tooth, spiraling out through the lip, up to 10 feet long.
comments: Best current thinking is that it senses water temperature and salinity. A tooth used as an instrument.
Good one to hand a kid who is deep in a unicorn phase → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/unicorn-of-the-sea/

posts.text: Every crested gecko in the pet trade descends from one population rediscovered in New Caledonia in 1994, during a tropical storm, after the species had been considered extinct for over a century. They also live 15 to 20 years, with the earliest captives reaching their 30s.
comments: That lifespan is the number worth sitting with before buying one. Cost breakdown here → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/crested-gecko-cost-guide/

posts.text: New Caledonian crows bend hooked tools out of twigs to fish grubs out of bark, then teach the technique to their young.
comments: Passing a method down a generation is the definition of culture. Birds have it.
For anyone on your feed who still says bird brain → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/crow-tool-users/

posts.text: Dolphins pass the mirror test, which puts them in a very short list with humans, great apes, and elephants.
comments: Recognizing yourself in a reflection is one of the few concrete handles we have on self-awareness.
Share it with whoever argues animals have no inner life → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/mirror-test-passers/

posts.text: Guinea pigs cannot make their own vitamin C, same as us, which makes deficiency a genuinely species-specific risk. It weakens the immune system, slows wound healing, and disrupts normal bone and tooth development.
comments: Respiratory infection is the urgent one, since guinea pigs are obligate nasal breathers and cannot switch to their mouth. Everything to watch for → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/guinea-pig-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Chameleons do not mainly change color to hide. They do it to communicate.
comments: The color tracks mood and social signaling. The camouflage version of the story is the one that stuck.
Pass it to the person who bought a chameleon to watch it match the couch → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/color-changing-camouflage/

posts.text: A mayfly can spend years developing underwater, then emerge, mate, and die the same day.
comments: Some adults last only hours. The entire visible life of the animal is the epilogue.
One to send someone having a long week → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/butterfly-birthdays/

posts.text: Budgies hide illness because prey animals do. By the time one looks visibly sick it is often further along than a mammal would be at the same point, which is why finding an avian vet before you need one actually matters.
comments: The single biggest preventable problem is the all-seed diet, which drives obesity and fatty liver disease. Full rundown → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/budgie-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Box turtles can pass 100 years old, and they can go months without eating.
comments: They drop into a hibernation-like state to stretch the energy. One of the longest-living pets anyone actually keeps.
For anyone about to buy a turtle without reading the lifespan → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/survival-specialists/

posts.text: An electric eel can put out 600 volts, enough to stun a horse.
comments: It uses it for hunting and for defense, in the rivers of the Amazon basin.
Send it to whoever is scared of the wrong river animal → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/electric-eel-shock/

posts.text: Russian tortoises are one of the more approachable tortoises to own, in price and in the fact that this one can live its whole life indoors. Hatchlings run $50 to $150, older captive-bred animals $225 to $400.
comments: An open-topped tortoise table, not an aquarium, is $125 to $200 of the setup on its own. Full costs → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/russian-tortoise-cost-guide/

posts.text: In 1945 a rooster named Miracle Mike lived over 18 months after his head came off. The axe missed the brain stem.
comments: He toured as a sideshow attraction. One of those stories that sounds invented and is not.
Nobody believes this one first time. Proof → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/miracle-mike-the-headless-rooster/

posts.text: The pen-tailed tree shrew drinks fermented palm nectar at roughly 3.8 percent alcohol, about beer strength, every day.
comments: Special metabolic enzymes keep it sober through all of it. A daily happy hour with no hangover.
For the friend who claims they can hold their drink → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/boozy-nectar-loving-shrew/

posts.text: A juvenile oscar costs $7 to $35. A 55-gallon starter setup has been estimated around $560 as a genuinely low-end build, and even that undersells what the fish actually needs.
comments: An aquarium retailer put it best: this fish can live as long as a dog. Full cost picture → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/oscar-fish-cost-guide/

posts.text: An ocean sunfish can lay 300 million eggs at once, more than any other vertebrate on earth.
comments: Almost none survive to adulthood. The entire strategy is volume.
Hand this to anyone who thinks they have a lot on → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/natures-biggest-gamble/

posts.text: A hedgehog can run 6 miles per hour, which is genuinely quick for something that size.
comments: The spines are the famous part, but they curl up for comfort as much as defense once they feel safe.
Send it to whoever wants one and thinks they are slow → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/cuddle-drones/

posts.text: A tiger salamander bought for $30 can outlive plenty of pets people treat as long-term commitments. A recognized longevity database puts the captive record at 25 years.
comments: Juveniles typically run $30 to $50, rarer morphs $125 or more. What the real budget looks like → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/tiger-salamander-cost-guide/

posts.text: A female sea turtle will travel thousands of miles to lay eggs on the same beach where she hatched.
comments: How she finds it after a decade at sea is still one of the better open questions in animal navigation.
For anyone who likes a genuinely unsolved mystery → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/egg-layers-of-mystery/
